examples.name: Hall bar
examples.summary: Four-terminal Hall bar: Hall resistance B/ne from the field model and from ballistic trajectories, swept in field.

examples.name: Two-terminal device (diffusive to ballistic)
examples.summary: A plain two-terminal strip: conductance against mean free path, from Ohm (G grows with l) to the Sharvin/Landauer ceiling.

examples.name: Quadratic device, four-point (van der Pauw)
examples.summary: A square with a contact in each corner: four-point resistance R = (ln2/pi) rho_s, independent of contact resistance.

examples.name: EMR, four-terminal with central shunt
examples.summary: Graphene square with a concentric metal disc: at B = 0 the current runs through the metal, in a field it is pushed around it - a huge geometric magnetoresistance.

examples.name: EMR, four-terminal with off-centre shunt
examples.summary: The central-shunt square with the metal disc moved off centre: the left-right mirror symmetry is broken, so R(B) is no longer even in B.

examples.name: EMR bar with side shunt (read-head geometry)
examples.summary: Solin's read-head bar: a metal shunt along one long edge, all four contacts on the opposite edge. Several hundred per cent MR at 1 T.

examples.name: Hydrodynamic device: negative vicinity resistance
examples.summary: Current injected from a side contact; the probe right next to it reads a NEGATIVE voltage in the viscous regime (Bandurin 2016).

examples.name: Hydrodynamic device: superballistic aperture
examples.summary: A slit in a wall: viscous flow through it can conduct MORE than the ballistic (Sharvin) limit, and more as temperature rises.

examples.name: Veselago lens (flat p-n junction)
examples.summary: A point source in front of a straight n-p junction: negative refraction refocuses the rays at the mirror point behind it.

examples.name: Dirac fermion microscope: beam onto a circular p-n junction
examples.summary: A collimated Dirac-electron beam aimed at a Veselago dot (a circular p-n junction): transparent at B = 0, a trap for whispering-gallery orbits at a few mT.

examples.name: Dirac fermion microscope: imaging a reflecting disc
examples.summary: Fig. 3c: the collimated beam is steered across a small reflecting disc with the magnetic field, and the target shows up as a dip in transmission.

examples.name: KT magnetometer (Klein-tunnelling p-n superlattice)
examples.summary: Alternating p and n stripes across a clean channel: Klein transmission is angle-selective, so a few mT of field changes the resistance strongly.
